document_title: The Every-day Life of Abraham Lincoln: A Narrative And Descriptive Biography With Pen-Pictures And Personal; Recollections By Those Who Knew Him
author: Francis F. Browne
claims: John Wilkes Booth was the assassin.
Booth ran towards the narrator after shouting 'The South shall be free.'
Booth escaped through a door in the rear of the theatre and mounted a horse.
The narrator did not know the President was shot at the time.
A woman's shriek pierced the theatre after the assassin's leap and flight.
Mrs. Lincoln pointed to the retreating figure and cried, 'He has killed the President!'
The audience experienced a mixture of horror, noises, and uncertainty.
The sound of a horse's hoofs clattering with speed was heard.
People broke chairs and railings in confusion.
Women fainted and feeble persons were trampled.
The stage filled with a dense crowd.
Actors and actresses were on stage in costume, showing fright.
Soldiers stormed the house after hearing what happened.
